Subject: [Acuity] Spike in P95 + intermittent 503s on our private VPC since kernel update

Jonas —

We started seeing a sustained jump in p95 latency across our inference endpoints beginning ~03:00 UTC this morning. The spike correlates with the maintenance window where your on-prem package applied the kernel-level optimizer patch last night. We're also observing intermittent 503s for a subset (~2-3%) of requests to the 'prompt-v2' model path. Attached: acuity_prod_p95_20260809.png and acuity_kv_logs_08_09.txt.

Impact: customer-facing clinical summarization flows taking 600-1200ms more at p95; occasional 503s cause retries in our client and visible UX errors. This is blocking our morning standups and the release we planned for Monday.

Asking for: immediate triage, a recommended mitigation (fallback to prior runtime or config change), and an exec sync if we need cross-org escalation. Happy to provide S3 access to full logs.

Thanks,
Daniel Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering — Acuity Labs

Subject: Re: [Acuity] Spike in P95 + intermittent 503s on our private VPC since kernel update

Quick triage update — I pulled the KV logs Daniel attached and correlated with our metrics. Preliminary findings:
- KV cache hit rate degraded ~18% at 02:55 UTC for the acuity cluster; prefix eviction frequency spiked.
- Batch size distribution shifted right (median batch size up ~22%) around the same time.
- Error traces show token decoding failures that produce 503 paths when worker queues exceed the soft limit.

Hypothesis: the kernel optimizer changed cache insertion/tombstone handling under high concurrency which increased prefix churn and caused more cache misses. That, combined with slightly larger batches, pushed some workers over the queue threshold.

Immediate mitigations I can push (non-disruptive):
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size in the acuity route to previous baseline (from 64 -> 44)
- Enable aggressive prefix prefetch TTL to boost hot-key retention
- Raise per-worker queue soft limit by 10% to avoid instant 503s while we monitor

I can roll these in a canary to one shard in 10 minutes and watch p95. If that doesn't help we should revert to the prior runtime build (last known good).

I'll start the canary after confirmation.

-Aditi (Aditya Rao)
Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Morning — brief status for execs:
- Incident: p95 latency increase (~+600-800ms) and intermittent 503s after kernel optimizer patch during maintenance window.
- Root cause (probable): increased KV prefix eviction and larger batch sizes caused by runtime patch interactions under Acuity's concurrency profile.
- Short-term remediation: rolled reduced max_batch_size and aggressive prefix prefetch; canary showed p95 improvement and KV hit recovery. Gradual rollout in progress; no new 503s reported.
- Next steps: 1) complete rollout and monitor for 6 hours; 2) follow up with a postmortem including config diff and suggested kernel parameter changes; 3) if we observe relapse, immediate rollback to prior runtime build (ticket INF-9123).

Laura — can you coordinate an executive lane call at 10:00 PT if Acuity wants an all-hands? Evelyn, please prepare a 1-pager for execs summarizing impact, mitigation, and rollback plan.

Daniel — appreciate the quick signal. We'll keep the line open and update you every 45 minutes while we finish the rollout.

Thanks,
Jonas
